title: unified-rollouts: composite-metric-driven-auto-rollback-for-shadow-canary-and-ab
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Adds composite-metric autorollback policy allowing weighted evaluation of latency, error-rate, and quality regressions for canary, A/B, and shadow rollouts; includes observability hooks and e2e tests.
description:
Motivation: As customers adopt progressive rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) across diverse workloads, single-metric rollback triggers (e.g. only 95th latency or only error-rate) lead to noisy rollbacks or missed regressions. This PR introduces a composite-metric autorollback policy that evaluates a weighted score derived from latency, error-rate, and quality regression signals to make rollback decisions, and wires it into unified rollouts for canary/A-B/shadow modes.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a new CompositeMetricPolicy in the rollouts controller that evaluates multiple metrics and computes a normalized score.
- Adds a configurable weighting and threshold model: teams can tune weightings for latency, error-rate, and quality; a single threshold triggers automated rollback.
- Extends shadow and canary pilot pipelines to emit the quality delta metric (promptset-based regression) used by the composite score.
- Adds observability: per-rollout composite_score metric, breakdown gauges for each component, and alerting-friendly tagging.
- Adds e2e tests and integration tests for staged shadow and A/B rollouts demonstrating policy behavior under noisy signals.

Design notes:
- Scores are normalized to a 0..100 scale per metric using empirically derived baselines and rolling windows. The CompositeMetricPolicy computes score = sum(w_i * normalized_i). A configured threshold (default 40) triggers an automatic rollback.
- To avoid hypersensitivity to transient noise, the policy supports configurable windowing (60s/5m/15m) and a minimum evaluation sample count.
- For quality regressions we reuse the promptset evaluation pipeline (redwood-evals integration) and emit a quality_delta metric (signed percent points).
- This policy is pluggable: rollout spec gains a new field rollout.policy.composite_metric with weights/threshold/window/sample_min. Backwards compatible: if absent, prior single-metric rules remain in effect.

Operational considerations:
- Default weights chosen conservatively (latency:0.4, error:0.4, quality:0.2) after internal benchmarking across LLM workloads.
- Added canary safety guard: auto-rollback will only trigger if canary traffic > configured min_traffic AND composite_score>threshold for at least two consecutive evaluation windows.
- Shadow rollouts: composite_score is computed from shadow probes and can be used to automatically stop subsequent promotion steps when above threshold.

Testing:
- Unit tests for normalization and scoring logic.
- Integration tests for rollout controller path with synthetic metric generators.
- Two e2e fixtures that simulate (1) latency spike with no quality regression and (2) small quality regression with stable latency; verifies policy respects weights.
- Ran full CI matrix including runtime bench job and perf-canary smoke tests.

Migration:
- No DB schema changes. Rollouts with no composite_metric field behave unchanged. Teams can opt-in by adding the policy to rollout specs or via new rollout presets in the Console.

Security/Privacy:
- No new customer data is captured beyond existing telemetry. Quality regressions are computed from promptset evals stored in evals service and referenced by rollout (no raw prompts are embedded into rollout objects).

Usage example (rollout spec snippet):
rollout:
  strategy: canary
  policy:
    type: composite_metric
    composite_metric:
      weights:
        latency: 0.4
        error_rate: 0.4
        quality: 0.2
      threshold: 40
      window: 300  # seconds
      min_samples: 50

Notes: This PR focuses on the controller, telemetry and tests; Console UI for editing weights will be a follow-up (ENG-518).

changelog_entry: Feature: Composite-metric autorollback policy for unified rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow) with observability and e2e tests. Opt-in via rollout.spec.policy.composite_metric.
support_guidance: If customers see noisy rollbacks, recommend increasing window/min_samples or lowering quality weight; default presets provided in Console once UI follow-up ships.
